summary: This trimmed snippet adds two numeric stream pipelines to the farmers' market app: one that totals the price of every product, and one that averages the price of only the organic products. Both use mapToDouble to turn a stream of products into a stream of plain double values that math methods can work on.

lines.text: The book trimmed this example down to just the new code, so the placeholder comment stands in for the product list built in the earlier exercises; the full listing is in your IDE.
A double sum can print with a long tail of decimals, so String.format with "%.2f" rounds the result to two places for display as money.

mapToDouble is the specialized version of map that produces a stream of primitive doubles rather than objects, which is what unlocks the math methods on the next line. The method reference MarketProduct::getPrice simply says "call getPrice on each product."
sum() is a terminal operation available only on a numeric stream; it consumes the doubles and hands back a single total, leaving the original product list untouched.
Filtering before mapping is the usual order: narrow the stream to the items you care about first, then transform only those fewer results.
average() cannot return a number when the stream is empty, so it hands back an OptionalDouble; orElse supplies 0.0 as the fallback rather than letting the code fail.
